        Restart never quits from within the click that asks for it. The
        click, on the notification's Restart or the Updates section's, only
        asks for a restart, and the restart begins once that click's handling
        is over and no window is being updated, in a later turn of the
        application's own loop, as any quit asked for from within the window
        does. So asking whether to quit, closing the window, putting the
        update in place, and starting Suspense again never touch a window
        while it is still being updated, and never panic for it, as GPUI does
        with "attempted to read a window that is already on the stack". The
        same holds for every way Suspense quits, Ctrl+Q, the palette's Quit,
        the window's close button, the quit dialog's Quit, and a restart
        from anywhere else, as the About panel's Check for Updates leads to:
        each asks for the quit and lets it run once the window it came from
        is free.

        The new Suspense is started only once the update is in place, and
        the running one then exits, its window closed and its work stopped
        as quitting stops it, never left running beside the new one. A
        restart that can't start the new binary, as where it won't run,
        leaves the update in place, says so in a notification with why,
        before quitting, rather than quitting with nothing started, and
        records it in the log. Nothing in a restart ever panics: a step that
        fails is reported and logged, and Suspense is left either running
        as it was, or quit with the update in place and the new one started.

tool_use_result.originalFile:
use /lib
from /scope/application/MainWindow import MainWindowScope
from /scope/edge-releases import EdgeReleasesScope
from /scope/open-file import OpenFileScope
from /scope/settings-window import SettingsWindowScope
from /scope/user-preferences import UserPreferencesScope

export scope SelfUpdateScope:
    concept: {SelfUpdateConcept}

concept SelfUpdateConcept:
    pitch:
        Suspense keeps itself up to date: it looks for a newer edge release,
        downloads it in the background, and puts it in place of its own
        binary when it restarts, so the newest build is only a restart away.

    shape: {SelfUpdateShape}

shape SelfUpdateShape:
    description:
        Updates come from the edge releases, as the @{EdgeReleasesScope}
        says, published in the GitHub repository the running build was
        published from, which it knows because that is baked into it. Only
        such a build updates itself. A build made anywhere else, as on a
        developer's machine, never looks for an update, never downloads one,
        and never replaces its binary, and the Updates section says why.

    checking:
        A check asks GitHub's releases API for the repository's releases,
        pre-releases included, and takes the one with the highest version
        `0.1.N`, comparing N as a number, never as text. It is newer only
        when its N is greater than the running build's; an older or equal one
        is never taken, so an update never goes back. A release without the
        asset for the running platform is passed over for the newest one
        that has it.

        Suspense checks a few seconds after it starts, and then every 6
        hours while it runs, in the background, never holding up anything
        else, and only while "Check for updates automatically" is on, as it
        is until turned off. That choice is remembered for the user, as the
        @{UserPreferencesScope} says. Check for updates, in the Updates
        section, checks straight away, whether it is on or not. A check that
        can't be made, as with no network or GitHub refusing it, is quiet
        when automatic, trying again at the next, and says why when asked
        for.

    downloading:
        A newer release found is downloaded straight away, in the background,
        taking the asset for the platform and architecture running,
        `suspense-0.1.N-linux-x86_64.tar.gz`, `suspense-0.1.N-windows-x86_64.zip`, or
        `suspense-0.1.N-macos-aarch64.tar.gz`. It is checked against the size
        GitHub gives for it, and against its SHA-256 digest where GitHub
        gives one, and one that doesn't match is thrown away and never used.
        The binary is taken out of the archive and staged beside the running
        binary, in the same directory, so it can be put in place by a rename,
        marked executable where the platform has such a mark. One download
        runs at a time; a newer release found while one is staged replaces
        it. A download that fails says so in the Updates section, and is
        tried again at the next check.

        Where the running binary's directory can't be written, nothing is
        downloaded, and the Updates section says that Suspense can't update
        itself there, with the directory, and a link to the release's page,
        opened in the browser, so it can be updated by hand.

    restarting:
        Once an update is staged, a notification says "Suspense 0.1.N is
        ready", with a Restart button and a Later button. The Updates section
        says the same, with a Restart button, for as long as it stays staged.
        Later only closes the notification; the update stays staged, and is
        put in place whenever Suspense next quits.

        Restart quits as quitting does, as the @{MainWindowScope} says,
        asking first while work is running, and doing nothing more if the
        quit is cancelled, then starts Suspense again from the same path once
        the update is in place. However Suspense quits, a staged update is
        put in place as it does: the staged binary is renamed over the
        running one, the running one renamed aside first where the platform
        won't replace a running binary, as on Windows. The binary set aside
        is deleted at the next launch. An update left staged by a quit that
        never finished, as a crash, is put in place at the next launch, before
        anything else, and takes effect at the launch after, the Updates
        section saying a restart finishes it.

        Putting an update in place never leaves Suspense without a binary:
        a step that fails puts back the binary that was there, and the
        Updates section says why it couldn't update.

    updatesSection:
        The @{SettingsWindowScope} has an "Updates" section. It says the
        running version, as "Suspense 0.1.42", and where it can't update
        itself, as for a build made elsewhere, why, and offers nothing else.
        Otherwise it shows a checkbox reading "Check for updates
        automatically", a "Check for updates" button, disabled while a check
        or download is under way, and a line saying where things stand:
        "Checking for updates…", "Suspense is up to date", checked when, as
        "Checked 5 minutes ago", "Downloading 0.1.N…" with how much has
        come, "Suspense 0.1.N is ready" with a Restart button, or, in the
        theme's error colour, why the last check, download, or update failed.

    requests:
        Every request to GitHub sends a User-Agent naming Suspense and its
        version, as "Suspense/0.1.42", since GitHub refuses requests without
        one, and asks for its JSON with `Accept: application/vnd.github+json`.
        A check asks for the repository's releases at
        `https://api.github.com/repos/<owner>/<name>/releases`, 100 to a page,
        so the newest edge release is never missed for being past the first
        page, and takes the highest N among the releases whose tag is
        `v0.1.N`, ignoring drafts and any release whose tag isn't of that
        form. An asset is downloaded from its `browser_download_url`,
        following GitHub's redirects to where it is stored, and its digest,
        given as `sha256:<hex>`, is compared without regard to case.

        GitHub's limit on requests made without signing in is respected: a
        check refused for it, with a 403 or 429 and its rate-limit headers,
        says so, "GitHub's rate limit was reached; try again after" and the
        time it resets, and an automatic check isn't tried again before then.
        Any other refusal says the status GitHub gave and its message, never
        only that the check failed.

    afterUpdate:
        An update that has been put in place is confirmed at the next
        launch: the version now running is compared with the one staged, and
        where they match, a notification says "Updated to Suspense 0.1.N",
        and the Updates section says so until the next check. Where they
        don't, as when the binary put in place still reports the old
        version, the Updates section says, in the theme's error colour, that
        the update to 0.1.N didn't take effect, and the same release is never
        downloaded and put in place again by itself, so an update can never
        loop, one restart after another; a Check for updates asked for by
        hand still tries it.

        The binary set aside is deleted at the next launch, and where it
        can't be yet, as on Windows while the process that ran it is still
        exiting, it is tried again at each launch after, never stopping the
        launch. A staged binary left beside the running one that is no newer
        than it is deleted rather than put in place.

    diagnostics:
        Suspense keeps a log of what updating does, `updates.log` in its own
        data directory, beside its preferences, as the
        @{UserPreferencesScope} keeps them: one line per step, with the time,
        each check with the repository and running version it checked for,
        the releases it found and the one it took or why it took none, each
        download with its asset, size, and digest check, each staging, each
        putting in place with its paths and how it went, and each launch's
        confirmation, every failure with its whole error. It keeps the last
        1,000 lines.

        The Updates section has a "Details" disclosure, collapsed to start
        with, that shows what updating rests on: the running version, the
        repository it updates from, or that it has none and so is not an edge
        build, the running binary's path and whether its directory can be
        written, the last check's time and the newest release it found, and
        what is staged, if anything, with a "Show log" button that opens
        `updates.log` as the @{OpenFileScope} opens a file, and a "Copy"
        button that puts all of it, with the log's last 50 lines, on the
        clipboard, for a bug report.

content.text:
The panic most likely comes from Restart quitting inside its own click handler.
